Revenue

Our total material sales were $79.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to $82.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of 4% with an increase in unit material volume of 9%. The decrease in material sales was primarily due to changes in customer mix and a $4.8 million unfavorable period-over-period change in the cumulative catch-up adjustment, primarily attributable to material fees as described below, partially offset by higher unit material volume.

•
Green emitter sales for the three months ended September 30, 2026, which include our yellow-green emitters, were $60.9 million as compared to $64.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, with unit material volumes increasing by 5%.
•
Red emitter sales for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $18.9 million as compared to $16.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, with unit material volumes increasing by 25%.

 

Revenue from royalty and license fees was $75.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to $53.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of 42%. The increase in royalty and license fees was primarily the result of a $9.5 million out-of-period adjustment during the three months ended September 30, 2025 that reduced royalty and license fees, higher unit material volume and changes in customer mix.

 

31

 

The total cumulative catch-up adjustment recorded to revenue arising from changes in estimates of transaction price, net was a reduction of $3.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to a net increase of $1.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the adjustment resulted from a decrease in the average price per gram, primarily due to product mix changes and higher anticipated demand forecasted over the respective remaining lives of certain customer contracts. For the three months ended September 30, 2025, the adjustment resulted from an increase in the average price per gram, primarily due to lower anticipated demand from certain customers over the respective remaining lives of their contracts.

Revenue from contract research services consists of revenue earned by Adesis, which provides support services on a contractual basis to third-party customers in the pharma, biotech, catalysis and other industries. Contract research services revenue was $5.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to $3.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of 43%. The increase in contract research services revenue was primarily due to increased specialty manufacturing customer demand at Adesis during the three months ended September 30, 2026.

Cost of sales

Cost of sales for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased by $7.6 million as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to higher sales volume, Adesis' cost of sales, and a $1.1 million increase in inventory reserve expense. As a result of the increase in revenue from royalty and license fees, partially offset by the increase in the cost of sales, gross margin for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased by $13.2 million as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025, with gross margin as a percentage of revenue decreasing to 73% from 75%.

Research and development

Research and development expenses were $36.3 million for both three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025.

Selling, general and administrative

Selling, general and administrative expenses increased to $20.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to $18.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in selling, general and administrative expenses was primarily due to an increase in employee-related costs and consulting expenses.

Amortization of acquired technology and other intangible assets

Amortization of acquired technology and other intangible assets decreased to $3.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to $4.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in amortization of acquired technology and other intangible assets was primarily due to the completion of amortization of the BASF patent portfolio in June 2026, partially offset by the acquisition of the Merck KGaA patent portfolio in January 2026. See Note 7 in Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for further discussion.

Patent costs

Patent costs increased to $2.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to $1.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The results in the current quarter reflected higher internal prosecution related costs.

Royalty and license expense

Royalty and license expense increased to $244,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to $170,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

Interest and other income, net

Interest income, net was $8.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to $10.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in interest income, net was primarily attributable to lower bond yields and reduced average investment balances on available-for-sale investments compared with the same period in 2025.

32

 

Other income, net primarily consisted of net investment gains and losses, net exchange gains and losses on foreign currency transactions and rental income. The increase in other income, net was due to a $28.9 million increase in the carrying value of our minority equity investment portfolio and a $7.2 million foreign exchange gain during the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to a $3.0 million investment gain on our marketable equity securities portfolio, partially offset by a $1.9 million foreign exchange loss during the three months ended September 30, 2025. Net exchange gains and losses on foreign currency are primarily caused by the fluctuation in the Korean won to the U.S. Dollar exchange rate and resulting remeasurement of a Korean won-denominated withholding tax receivable.

The $8.5 million unfavorable period-over-period change in the cumulative catch-up adjustment was primarily attributable to product mix changes forecasted over the respective remaining lives of certain customer contracts.

•
Green emitter sales for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, which include our yellow-green emitters, were $175.8 million as compared to $191.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, with unit material volumes decreasing by 1%.

The $11.1 million favorable period-over-period change in the cumulative catch-up adjustment was primarily attributable to an increase in the average royalty and license fees price per gram due to lower anticipated demand from certain customers over the respective remaining lives of their contracts.

As a result of the decrease in revenue from material sales, partially offset by the increase in revenue from royalty and license fees, gross margin for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 decreased by $26.0 million as compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025, with gross margin as a percentage of revenue decreasing to 74% from 76%.

Liquidity and Capital Resources

Our principal sources of liquidity are our cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments. As of September 30, 2026, we had cash and cash equivalents of $93.4 million, short-term investments of $340.0 million, and long-term U.S. Government bonds investments of $394.6 million for a total of $828.0 million. This compares to cash and cash equivalents of $138.4 million, short-term investments of $464.0 million, and long-term U.S. Government bond investments of $353.0 million for a total of $955.4 million as of December 31, 2025.

Cash provided by operating activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $234.1 million resulting from $164.3 million of net income, $37.2 million from non-cash items including depreciation, stock-based compensation, amortization of intangibles and investment gains, net, and a $32.6 million increase due to changes in our operating assets and liabilities. Changes in our operating assets and liabilities related to a decrease in accounts receivable of $30.8 million, an increase in deferred revenue of $15.1 million and a decrease in inventory of $4.0 million, partially offset by an increase in other assets of $11.5 million, a decrease in other liabilities of $3.9 million and a decrease in accounts payable and accrued expenses of $1.9 million. The decrease in accounts receivable during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily due to the timing of material shipments as well as license fee payments from certain customers. The increase in deferred revenue during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily due to the timing of customer payments and revenue recognition.

Cash provided by operating activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 was $179.7 million resulting from $175.7 million of net income and $53.1 million from non-cash items including stock-based compensation, depreciation and amortization of intangibles, partially offset by a $49.1 million reduction due to changes in our operating assets and liabilities. Changes in our operating assets and liabilities related to an increase in other assets of $49.3 million, an increase in inventory of $29.7 million, a decrease in deferred revenue of $8.7 million and a decrease in other liabilities of $1.1 million, partially offset by a decrease in accounts receivable of $39.4 million and an increase in accounts payable of $304,000. The increase in other assets during the nine months ended September 30, 2025 was primarily due to an increase in unbilled receivables from certain customers. The decrease in accounts receivable during the nine months ended September 30, 2025 was primarily due to the timing of material shipments as well as license fee payments from certain customers. The increase in inventory during the nine months ended September 30, 2025 was primarily due to purchases of certain strategic raw materials.

Cash used in investing activities was $10.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to cash used in investing activities of $85.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in cash used in investing activities was due to timing of maturities and purchases of investments resulting in net sales and maturities of $47.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to net purchases of $44.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, partially offset by an increase in purchases of intangibles and property and equipment of $17.1 million. The increase in the purchases of intangibles during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily due to the acquisition of the Merck KGaA patent portfolio in January 2026.

35

 

Cash used in financing activities was $268.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to $72.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was due to an increase in the repurchases of common stock, inclusive of excise tax, of $193.0 million, an increase in the cash payment of dividends in the current year of $5.1 million and a decrease in the proceeds from issuance of common stock of $102,000, partially offset by a decrease in the payment of withholding taxes related to stock-based compensation to employees of $1.7 million.

Working capital was $781.2 million as of September 30, 2026, as compared to $979.0 million as of December 31, 2025. The decrease was primarily due to decreases in short-term investments, cash and cash equivalents and accounts receivable.

We anticipate, based on our internal forecasts and assumptions relating to our operations (including, among others, assumptions regarding our working capital requirements, the progress of our research and development efforts, the availability of sources of funding for our research and development work, and the timing and costs associated with the preparation, filing, prosecution, maintenance, defense and enforcement of our patents and patent applications), that we have sufficient cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments to meet our obligations for at least the next twelve months.

Additional funding may be required in the future for research, development and commercialization of our OLED technologies and materials, to obtain, maintain and enforce patents respecting these technologies and materials, and for working capital and other purposes, the timing and amount of which are difficult to ascertain. We believe that potential additional financing sources for us include long-term and short-term borrowings and public and private sales of our equity and debt securities. There can be no assurance that additional funds will be available to us when needed, on commercially reasonable terms or at all, particularly in the current economic environment.

ITEM 3. QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES ABOUT MARKET RISK

We do not utilize financial instruments for trading purposes and hold no derivative financial instruments, other financial instruments or derivative commodity instruments that could expose us to significant market risk other than our investments disclosed in “Fair Value Measurements” in Note 4 to the Consolidated Financial Statements. We generally invest in investment grade financial instruments to reduce our exposure related to investments. Our primary market risk exposure with regard to such financial instruments is to changes in interest rates, which would impact interest income earned on investments. However, based upon the conservative nature of our investment portfolio and current experience, we do not believe a decrease in investment yields would have a material negative effect on our interest income.

36

 

Substantially all our revenue is derived from outside of North America and primarily denominated in U.S. dollars and therefore we bear no significant foreign exchange risk from routine customer sales transactions. However, due to a withholding tax receivable denominated in Korean won, we do bear foreign exchange risk from fluctuations in the Korean won to U.S. dollar exchange rate and resulting remeasurement.

PART II – OTHER INFORMATION

ITEM 1. LEGAL PROCEEDINGS

Patent Related Challenges and Oppositions

Each major jurisdiction in the world that issues patents provides both third parties and applicants an opportunity to seek a further review of an issued patent. The process for requesting and considering such reviews is specific to the jurisdiction that issued the patent in question, and generally does not provide for claims of monetary damages or a review of specific claims of infringement. The conclusions made by the reviewing administrative bodies tend to be appealable and generally are limited in scope and applicability to the specific claims and jurisdiction in question.

We believe that opposition proceedings are frequently commenced in the ordinary course of business by third parties who may believe that one or more claims in a patent do not comply with the technical or legal requirements of the specific jurisdiction in which the patent was issued. We view these proceedings as reflective of its goal of obtaining the broadest legally permissible patent coverage permitted in each jurisdiction. Once a proceeding is initiated, as a general matter, the issued patent continues to be presumed valid until the jurisdiction’s applicable administrative body issues a final non-appealable decision. Depending on the jurisdiction, the outcome of these proceedings could include affirmation, denial or modification of some or all of the originally issued claims. We believe that as OLED technology becomes more established and its patent portfolio increases in size, so will the number of these proceedings.

ITEM 5. OTHER INFORMATION

Trading Arrangements

During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, none of our directors or executive officers adopted or terminated a “Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement” or “non-Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement,” as each term is defined in Item 408(a) of Regulation S-K.

SERP Amendment

On October 27, 2026, the Company’s Board of Directors (the “Board”), on the recommendation of its Human Capital Committee (the “HCC”), adopted Amendment 2026-1 to the SERP (“Amendment 2026-1”). Amendment 2026-1 amended the SERP to change the designated retirement age from age 65 to age 62, and to provide that persons who are at least age 62 but less than age 65 at the time of their qualifying termination or death, and who have at least 15 but less than 20 years of service, will receive prorated benefits as described in Amendment 2026-1. This change affects only one named executive officer participant in the SERP, Mauro Premutico, the Company’s Senior Vice President, Planning, Chief Legal Officer and Secretary, as all other named executive officer participants in the SERP are at least age 65.

Senior Management Severance Program

Also on October 27, 2026, the Board adopted a Senior Management Severance Program (the “SMSP”). Participants in the SERP are not eligible to participate in the SMSP. Thus, the only named executive officer who will participate in the SMSP is Brian Millard, the Company’s Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer. Participants in the SMSP are entitled to receive, following termination without cause, including a termination for good reason (both as defined in the SMSP), amounts including the following: (i) earned salary through the termination date; (ii) accrued but unpaid bonus for a completed year; (iii) a severance payment equal to twelve months of base salary plus the full year bonus that would have been earned for the year in which termination occurs based on actual performance as measured at the conclusion of the applicable year. The SMSP benefits shall not duplicate any payments to which the executive may become entitled under the executive’s change in control agreement. The benefits specified in clauses (ii) and (iii) above will vest 25%/year over four years, with the Board having the discretion to accelerate upon a separation event.
